t.1.25.1: Having heard the sage's resolute, unfaltering words, Rāghava, son of the best of men, firm in his vows, joined his palms in reverence and replied.
t.1.25.2: By the direction of my father's word, and out of reverence for my father's word, the word of Kauśika must be carried out without hesitation.
t.1.25.3: In Ayodhyā, in the midst of the elders, I was instructed by my great-souled father Daśaratha, and that word of his is not to be disregarded.
t.1.25.4: Having heard my father's word, I, at the command of this expounder of the Veda, shall carry out the excellent slaying of Tāṭakā; of this there is no doubt.
t.1.25.5: For the welfare of cows and brāhmaṇas and for the happiness of this land, I stand ready to carry out the command of you, whose greatness is immeasurable.
t.1.25.6: Having spoken thus, the subduer of foes clenched his fist around the middle of the bow and made a fierce twang of the bowstring, filling the directions with the sound.
t.1.25.7: By that sound the dwellers of Tāṭakā's forest were terrified, and Tāṭakā, bewildered by that sound, became furious.
t.1.25.8: Hearing that sound and attending closely to it, the rākṣasī, overcome with rage, rushed swiftly toward the place from which the sound had come.
t.1.25.9: Seeing her enraged, misshapen, with a distorted face and grown exceedingly huge in size, Rāghava spoke to Lakṣmaṇa.
t.1.25.10: Behold, Lakṣmaṇa, the terrible and dreadful form of the Yakṣiṇī; at the very sight of her the hearts of the timid would break apart.
t.1.25.12: For I cannot bring myself to kill her, protected as she is by her womanhood. Rather, I will destroy her might and her power of movement; such is my resolve.
t.1.25.11: Behold this one, hard to assail and endowed with the power of illusion; today I shall make her turn back, with her ears and the tip of her nose cut off.
t.1.25.13: But while Rāma was speaking thus, Tāṭakā, overcome with rage, raised both her arms and, roaring, rushed straight at Rāma.
t.1.25.14: As she came rushing at him with great speed, mighty like a thunderbolt, he pierced her in the chest with an arrow; she fell and died.
t.1.25.15: Seeing her, terrible in appearance, slain, the lord of the gods and the gods then honored Kākutstha, crying, "Well done, well done!"
t.1.25.16: The thousand-eyed Puraṃdara, supremely pleased, spoke, and then all the gods, greatly delighted, addressed Viśvāmitra.
t.1.25.17: O sage, may good fortune rest upon you, Kauśika; all the hosts of the Maruts, together with Indra, are pleased by this deed. Show your affection toward Rāghava.
t.1.25.18: O Brahmin, present to Rāghava the sons of the Prajāpati Bhṛśāśva, whose valour is true and who are endowed with the power of austerity.
t.1.25.20: Having spoken thus, all the gods, delighted, honored Viśvāmitra and departed the way they had come. Then twilight set in.
t.1.25.19: He has become a worthy recipient for you, O brahman, and is steadfast in following you; and a great deed on behalf of the gods is yet to be done by this son of the king.
t.1.25.21: Then the foremost of sages, pleased and gratified by the slaying of Tāṭakā, kissed Rāma on the head and spoke these words.
t.1.25.22: Let us spend the night here today, O Rāma of auspicious appearance; tomorrow at daybreak we shall go to that hermitage of mine.
